label: thm:main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:main}
The Tur\'an density of the tetrahedron satisfies
\[
  \pi(K_4^{(3)})\;\le\;\frac{14993367693127837}{26880000000000000}\;<\;0.557789.
\]
head: environment
name: main bound

label: lem:chain
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:chain}
For all $F\in\mathcal F^\sigma_m$, $G\in\mathcal F^\sigma_n$ and $m\le\ell\le n$,
\[
  p(F;G)\;=\;\sum_{F'\in\mathcal F^\sigma_\ell}p(F;F')\,p(F';G).
\]
head: environment
name: chain rule

label: thm:limits
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:limits}
The elements of $\operatorname{Hom}^+(\mathcal A^\sigma,\mathbb R)$ are exactly the limits of
convergent sequences $\{G_n\}$ of $\sigma$-flags, with
$\phi(F)=\lim_{n\to\infty}p(F;G_n)$ for every $F\in\mathcal F^\sigma$.
head: environment

label: lem:coeffbound
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: coefficient bound

title: Proof
body_md:
For every $\phi\in\operatorname{Hom}^+(\mathcal A^\sigma,\mathbb R)$, positivity and
\eqref{eq:unit} give
\[
  \phi(f)=\sum_{F\in\mathcal F^\sigma_\ell}c_F\phi(F)
  \;\le\;\Bigl(\max_{F\in\mathcal F^\sigma_\ell}c_F\Bigr)
    \sum_{F\in\mathcal F^\sigma_\ell}\phi(F)
  \;=\;\max_{F\in\mathcal F^\sigma_\ell}c_F .\qedhere
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For each $n\ge3$, choose a $K_4^{(3)}$-free $3$-graph $G_n$ on $n$
vertices with $\operatorname{ex}(n,K_4^{(3)})$ edges.  Since $\mathcal F^0$ is countable
and every density lies in $[0,1]$, a diagonal argument gives a
subsequence along which $p(F;G_n)$ converges for every $F\in\mathcal F^0$.
By \cref{thm:limits}, these limits define a positive homomorphism
$\psi$ with $\psi(\rho)=\pi(K_4^{(3)})$.
Conversely, every $\phi\in\operatorname{Hom}^+(\mathcal A^0,\mathbb R)$ is realized by a
convergent sequence $\{G'_n\}$ with $|V(G'_n)|\to\infty$.
Taking limits in
\[
  p(\rho;G'_n)\le
  \frac{\operatorname{ex}(|V(G'_n)|,K_4^{(3)})}{\binom{|V(G'_n)|}{3}}
\]
gives $\phi(\rho)\le\pi(K_4^{(3)})$.
head: environment

label: thm:downward
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:downward}
If $f\ge0$ in $\mathcal A^\sigma$, then $\left\llbracket f\right\rrbracket_\sigma\ge0$ in $\mathcal A^0$.
head: environment

label: prop:maxstat
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\pi^1\colon\mathcal A^0\to\mathcal A^1$ and $\partial_1\colon\mathcal A^0\to\mathcal A^1$
be Razborov's upward operator and vertex differential, respectively
\cite[\S\S2.3.1 and~4.3]{Razborov2007}.  For $M\in\mathcal F^0_\ell$,
$\pi^1(M)$ is the sum of the $1$-flags on $\ell+1$ vertices whose
non-root vertices induce a copy of $M$.  For the hyperedge,
$\partial_1\rho=3(\pi^1(\rho)-d)$, so \cite[Theorem~2.8(a)]{Razborov2007}
gives
\[
  \left\llbracket d\cdot\partial_1\rho\right\rrbracket_1
  =3\bigl(\rho\cdot\left\llbracket d\right\rrbracket_1-\left\llbracket d\cdot d\right\rrbracket_1\bigr)=S .
\]
Razborov calls a theory \emph{vertex uniform} if it has exactly one
one-vertex type \cite[Definition~11]{Razborov2007}.  This condition
holds for $\mathcal{T}$, since the only $3$-graph on a single vertex has no
edges.  We can therefore apply the stationarity criterion of Razborov
\cite[Corollary~4.6(a)]{Razborov2007}.  At an edge-density maximizer
$\phi_0$, take $M_1=\rho$, the objective $f(t)=-t$ on $\mathbb R$, and
$g=d$.  The choice $f(t)=-t$ makes $\phi_0$ a minimizer of the
objective in that corollary.  It gives
$\phi_0(\left\llbracket d\cdot\partial_1\rho\right\rrbracket_1)=0$, hence $\phi_0(S)=0$.
head: environment

label: prop:certificate-bound
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:certificate-bound}
If $Q_b\succeq 0$ for every block and the coefficients in
\eqref{eq:certificate-coefficient} satisfy $c_G\le B$ for every
$G\in\mathcal F^0_m$, then $\pi(K_4^{(3)})\le B$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By \cref{prop:attained}, choose a maximizer $\phi$ with
$\phi(\rho)=\pi(K_4^{(3)})$.  By \cref{prop:maxstat},
$\phi(\tau S)=0$ for every $\tau\in\mathbb R$, while each quadratic-form
contribution is nonnegative by \cref{thm:downward}.  Applying $\phi$ to
\eqref{eq:certificate} and using \cref{lem:coeffbound} gives
\[
  \pi(K_4^{(3)})=\phi(\rho)
  \le\phi\!\left(\rho+
    \sum_b\left\llbracket \mathbf F_b^{\mathsf T}Q_b\mathbf F_b\right\rrbracket_{\sigma_b}
    +\tau S\right)
  \le\max_{G\in\mathcal F^0_m}c_G\le B.\qedhere
\]
head: environment

label: prop:seven-certificate
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:seven-certificate}
For the blocks, integer factor vectors, and stationarity multiplier
specified above, set
\[
  L=5040M^2=322{,}560{,}000{,}000{,}000{,}000,
  \qquad C_7(G)=L\,c_G,
\]
where $c_G$ is given by \eqref{eq:ansatz}.
Then, $C_7(G)\in\mathbb Z$ for every $G\in\mathcal F^0_7$, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:maxcol}
  \max_{G\in\mathcal F^0_7}C_7(G)=179{,}920{,}412{,}317{,}534{,}044.
\end{equation}
Consequently, these data form an exact certificate with
\[
  \max_{G\in\mathcal F^0_7}c_G=\frac{14993367693127837}{26880000000000000}=B.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The factorization of each $Q_b$ is a sum of outer products of
rational vectors, so $Q_b\succeq 0$.
For the block sizes $(s_b,\ell_b)=(1,4),(3,5),(4,5),(5,6)$,
the average in \eqref{eq:coefficient-matrix} runs over, respectively,
$140$, $1260$, $5040$, and $5040$ equally weighted choices of
root-label assignments and ordered pairs of disjoint non-root sets.
All four numbers divide
$5040$.  The two averages in \eqref{eq:stationarity-coefficient}
have respectively $140$ and $630$ equally likely choices, which
also divide $5040$.  Since the edge-density denominator is $35$
and $M^2\tau$ is an integer, \eqref{eq:ansatz} implies
$C_7(G)\in\mathbb Z$.

To verify \eqref{eq:maxcol}, we take one representative of each of
the $964$ tetrahedron-free $3$-graphs on six vertices, add one
vertex, and consider all $2^{15}$ choices of edges containing it.
Retaining the tetrahedron-free extensions gives a list covering
every member of $\mathcal F^0_7$ up to isomorphism: deleting any vertex
from such a $3$-graph leaves a member of the six-vertex catalog.
Repeated isomorphism classes do not affect the maximum.
The exhaustive integer evaluations detailed in
Appendix~\ref{app:exact-verification} establish \eqref{eq:maxcol}
on this list; the counting formulas are given in
Appendix~\ref{sec:coeff}.
Dividing the maximum by $L$ gives $B=\frac{14993367693127837}{26880000000000000}$.
Together with the rational factorizations, this proves that the
data form the claimed exact certificate.

label: prop:type-symmetry
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix one such set $U$.  Every labeling with image $U$ that induces
$\sigma$ differs from $\theta_U$ by a unique automorphism of
$\sigma$.  Hence
\[
 \sum_{\substack{\theta([5])=U\\\theta\text{ induces }\sigma}}
 (Q_b)_{i(\theta,x_U),i(\theta,y_U)}
 =\sum_{g\in\operatorname{Aut}(\sigma)}(Q_b)_{g\cdot i_U,g\cdot j_U}
 =(\widehat Q_b)_{i_U,j_U}.
\]
Summing over all such $U$ gives \eqref{eq:fiveorbit}.
Changing $\theta_U$ only permutes the automorphisms in the sum,
so the value is independent of the chosen labeling.  It is also
unchanged when $x_U$ and $y_U$ are interchanged, since $\widehat Q_b$
is symmetric.
